subject: MAT
label: Grade 12 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Science Mathematics, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 7 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Relations, functions and inverse trigonometric functions
modules.outcome: define and graph functions and their inverses
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Relations, functions and inverse trigonometric functions', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: define and graph functions and their inverses. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Show it with objects or a picture: build or draw the idea in 'Relations, functions and inverse trigonometric functions' before using symbols.
Say the rule in your own words, then write one worked line, naming each step.
Use it: define and graph functions and their inverses. Start with one easy question, then one with a real-life story.
Check it: use a second method, estimate, or work backwards to test your answer.
modules.example: Model run for 'Relations, functions and inverse trigonometric functions'. Read the question and underline what is asked. Draw or write what is known. Choose the method named in the unit. Work it line by line, one idea per line, with units where they apply. Estimate first so the answer can be tested for sense. Check by working backwards. What a good answer looks like: correct method, every step visible, units stated, and a one-line check.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Define and graph functions and their inverses: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Relations, functions and inverse trigonometric functions), and at which Bloom level is it?
'define', at the Apply level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 7 (Linear programming and probability) run?
Weeks 32 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: count, add and subtract small numbers; name shapes.
L2: use the four operations, fractions and simple measures.
L3: work with ratio, algebra beginnings and geometry reasoning.
L4: algebra, geometry proof, trigonometry and statistics.
L5: functions, calculus, vectors and probability.
L6 (degree): proof, linear algebra and modelling.
L7 (postgraduate): research mathematics, data science or teaching at depth.
